findings.text: FDPIC ELF core dump entry consumes coredump parameters and reports whether header preparation completed, producing a file with header plus segment descriptors plus notes plus memory images.

Dump collects per thread status for queued dumpers then current, counts headers from area count plus arch extras plus one notes entry, sizes process info and auxiliary vector notes, lays out header then descriptors then notes then page aligned data, emits in that order followed by arch extra data and optional extended numbering record, then releases temporaries.

Transmitted header count is capped when total exceeds the extended numbering threshold, with overflow preserved in a separate section header record; file offsets advance through notes size and per area dump sizes and arch extra sizes.

Notes are emitted as first thread primary note then process info then auxiliary vector then remaining notes of first thread then all notes of other threads; auxiliary vector length is found by scanning value pairs for terminator and its size is added to notes total.

Per area segment descriptors carry load type, file offset, virtual start, zero physical address, dump size versus full span, page alignment, and readable writable executable flags derived from area protection flags.

All allocation and emission failures converge on one exit path that frees thread list and header and info and extended numbering records; success marker is set after header setup so early failures return not dumped; final file position is compared against computed offset with a warning on mismatch.
Library table holds a fixed array sized by the shared library limit, each slot recording code start, data start, break start, text length, entry address, build date, and a loaded flag.
Data alignment is 32. Stack alignment is the larger of pointer size and architecture minimum. Chunk buffer size is 4000.
Relocation failure sentinel is 0xff00ff01. Unloaded library placeholder is 0x7ff000ff. Maximum shared libraries is 1.
One configuration defines data start offset words and library count update as zero; the other configuration defines both as the shared library limit.
Gzip header flag bits are ASCII 0x01, continuation 0x02, extra field 0x04, original name 0x08, comment 0x10, encrypted 0x20, reserved 0xC0.
Relocate address helper is identity on its argument. Log prefix helper prepends module name to a format.
Flat loader registers a binary format object associating this module with the flat binary load callback.

Stack table creation reserves slots for environment and argument vectors plus optional vector bases plus count, aligns the stack base down, stores count and optional bases, then writes argument pointers followed by terminator and environment pointers followed by terminator while recording argument and environment address ranges.
Stack table writes that fault return a fault status; empty or overlong argument or environment strings return an invalid status.

Compressed execution loader allocates inflate workspace and read chunk, reads leading bytes, checks size and magic and method and forbidden flags, skips optional extra and name and comment fields with bounds checks, initializes raw inflate, then inflates incrementally while refilling input from file until completion.

Decompression returns no memory when workspace or chunk allocation fails and not executable for header validation failures; buffer overruns, inflate initialization failure, and negative inflate status abort; workspace and chunk and inflate state are always released.

Relocation calculation rejects offsets beyond combined data extent plus text length with an error log and segmentation signal and failure sentinel; smaller offsets map into text base and larger valid offsets map into data base after subtracting text length.

Old style relocation fetches a word from a data relative user address, or code relative on one architecture, adds code base or data base or data end according to old text data or bss type, warns on unknown type, and writes the result back.

Global offset table skip applies only on one architecture: two leading all ones words skip four slots, one leading all ones word skips two slots, otherwise or on read failure the pointer is unchanged.

Flat file load interprets header lengths and counts and flags and revision in network order, requires expected magic and supported revision and sane field widths and enabled compression support and data plus bss within data limit, then begins new execution and sets personality and new exec state.

Mapping chooses ROM text with separate RAM data when no memory management and neither RAM nor compressed flag is set, otherwise unified RAM mapping; sizes include extra slack and offset words with page alignment and data alignment, content is read or inflated into place, descriptor code data and break boundaries and slot zero library record and masked entry plus build date are recorded.
Pre execution validation failures return before teardown; mapping allocation failures and content read failures unmap what was created; zero or error mapping results are treated as no memory.
